released.summary: Croki is a founder-focused ADE where native coding-agent Threads remain the durable execution spine and project work stays inspectable through files, terminal, preview, Git, checkpoints, Review, Senses, and child Threads.
product: Configured Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, and OpenClaw providers retain their native behavior by default.
Parallel workers persist as read-only child Threads beneath one canonical founder conversation.
Croki Senses derives bounded project perception from real Thread and runtime activity.
Founder Mode explicitly joins product reality, implementation, customer evidence, market direction, positioning, and distribution for one turn.
gtm: Croki is for founders building real software with coding agents.
The credible promise is one coherent environment for directing, inspecting, verifying, and shipping native agent work.
Product and market claims must remain tied to observed behavior and source provenance.
learnings: Canvas is useful as an automatic projection, not as manually maintained project memory or a second workflow system.
Delegated work must remain inspectable without creating another task database or writable conversation surface.
Project perception must be derived on demand rather than delaying startup with a second persistent cache.

building.intent: Make Croki's core Thread loop more natural to direct, easier to navigate, and safer under long-running daily use while preserving native provider behavior.
product: Add native realtime Codex voice beside the Thread composer with honest connection, listening, stopping, failure, and typing-fallback states.
Keep durable worker Threads nested beneath their canonical parent and make worker transcripts explicitly read-only.
Generate durable initial Thread titles and let the founder regenerate a weak generated title without overwriting a manual rename.
Bound Thread replay and renderer memory growth so long-running projects remain usable.
Keep pull requests, dedicated worktrees, preview actions, terminal history, and close shortcuts tied to the Thread the founder is actually operating.
Carry released-to-building application lineage into every provider turn without changing native behavior.
gtm: Strengthen the credible promise that one founder can direct, inspect, recover, and ship agent work from one environment.
Keep claims tied to released evidence while allowing the 0.4.7 candidate to remain explicitly unpublished.
Keep publication destinations independently gated under Croki ownership.
successSignals: A Codex Thread can start and stop an audio-only realtime session while typing remains available after every failure.
Worker Threads remain grouped with their parent across active, snoozed, and settled rail states and route back to the parent conversation.
Generated titles survive restart and can be regenerated from the current conversation without replacing a manual title.
Long Thread catch-up does not require full-database hydration or unbounded sidebar subscriptions.
The Croki ownership check, release smoke test, affected package tests, typechecks, and desktop production build pass before publication.
